title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers

target_networks.name: small transformers / language models up to 7B
game-playing networks written from zeros (Breakout, Go)

domain: benchmarking LLM agents on weight reading, repair, synthesis, infeasibility detection and data-free compression
tasks_benchmarks: WeightBench 42 tasks: TR-01 READ (10), TR-02 FIX (13), TR-03 META (5), TR-04 WRITE (6), TR-05 SYSTEMS (8)

notes_for_review: First benchmark that tries to separate weight-level reasoning from trial-and-error by metering forward passes and quarantining runs that use gradients or execution, with non-agentic baselines and reference solutions per task. Results show reading and writing small networks works but LLM patching and infeasibility detection stay near baseline, which tempers the MIT claims. Sample sizes are very small (1-2 runs per task, one seed), quarantine rates are high (e.g., 11 of 77 Opus runs, 13 of 42 DeepSeek runs), and about half of the reference solutions need privileged gradient access. The FIX track includes reasoning-loop repair tasks on small language models that resemble MIT's loop edit, but MIT's Qwen MATH-500 edit is not itself re-run.
